independence_statement: I read only the supplied CONVENTIONS.md, assigned scan026 boxes TSV and the assigned whole scan026 JPG, plus crops that I generated myself from that JPG. I did not read any witness, existing transcription, first reading, other reader crop, proposal, note or finding. No OCR, recognition library, external research, or TeX compilation was used. Every reading was made by visual inspection of image ink. All original-coordinate boxes were enlarged to 3000 pixels wide with LANCZOS; autocontrast was applied. Rotation values are Pillow degrees, positive counterclockwise. The whole source image was also viewed for layout.

boxes.concrete_visible_stroke_evidence: Two isolated numerals: left has an upper curve, diagonal descent and long basal stroke; right has a detached arched top and descending stem. Read as 25. No enclosing cancellation.

Opening and closing parentheses are distinct. The two repeated compressed words each have a shallow entry, low connected middle and a final descender; resp. is preferred but doubtful. The following first adjective is mostly horizontal with a high terminal tooth, hence tentative ouvert. loc. has an ascender and loop; fin. has a long crossed f and a final dot. Final word has a dotted entry and a tall middle stroke, allowing idem/item. Nothing is cancelled here.

The initial short group has dark overlapping loops and a horizontal stroke through its baseline. It may be cancelled su or simply an overwritten su; both the state and the letters are left uncertain. After it, the separate tall triangular b, looped d, dotted i forms, and the low terminal ion are visible. No replacement su has been silently supplied.

S is at upper left and a looped capital L at upper right. The horizontal arrow has an open hook at its left end and a right-pointing terminal. Two vertical arrows descend from S to I and I to J. Labels p and phi are to their left; both right labels read surj., with descenders and terminal dots. The final isolated curved mark at lower right is retained as a comma. Partial ink at the upper left is adjacent prose, not a fourth node.

Clockwise rotation makes the marginal lines approximately horizontal. Attention has two tall initial strokes; phi has a loop and downward tail. bijective has a descending j; iso is short and dotted. The parenthesized passage has d'ordre, a doubled f in diff., an isolated capital I, and a clearly looped plus followed by fine. The relation F <= G has a retraced left angle and separate lower bar, while F != G has a diagonal through equality. The clause after et is compressed; pourtant is only a candidate, and its long crossed terminal could be mistaken for an arrow. The following equals-like sign and relation are doubtful. The cancelled word before R_F has a looped ascender and a dotted short stroke, tentatively dite. Both relation subscripts and the final |F| = |G| are visible. Main-line en posant beneath the margin is excluded from this margin reading.

After rotation the central formula has F at left, a heavily retraced less-than angle with a detached lower bar, and G at right. The dot before G is associated with ink density or the preceding line, not a multiplication sign. Adjacent plus above and partial relation text below are not target formula content.

A thick single horizontal cancellation crosses the entire short word. Below and above it remain a left loop with ascender, an i-like short stroke and a possible terminal te. Preferred dite, alternative dit; the cancellation state is clear although the middle letters are obscured.

The prose begins with a looped e and low n. The next word has p, a closed o, curved s, a small a, and an extended terminal nt with a crossed t. Its last stroke is part of posant, not an independent arrow. The formula has a small circular q with descender, two equality strokes, a phi loop and a final p with long descender. A full stop follows. The small equality strokes higher at left belong to the diagonal marginal note.

Proposition is underlined by one long stroke. The next word begins with a looped capital S and ends with a high t, read Soient. F and G are separated by a comma; deux has a looped d; figures has a tall descending f and a final dot. The bottom edge contains fragments of the next line only.

The crop was turned counterclockwise 90 degrees for inspection. In source orientation a long, almost vertical marginal stroke descends and splits into two short diverging legs near its foot. There is no writing and no distinct arrowhead. The TikZ reproduces the original upright orientation, not the display rotation.

The item label is a) with an overwritten a-like loop. Pour que, raffine, and sous-figure have connected letters, including the long crossed f strokes. After il the abbreviated sequence f et s is visible; no expanded faut or suffit is supplied. The last line has G prime, de and G. The beginning of subdivision contains an anomalously long crossed stem between su and the triangular b; a cancelled f before b is preferred but simple b is retained as an alternative. No whole-passage cancellation crosses this item.

The start has a small angular s and a low u. A very tall stroke with a long lower loop/crossing precedes a separate triangular b-like form. This is tentatively an abandoned f followed by b, but it may be one overwritten b. The following division is clear through the looped d, i dots, and low terminal n. The doubtful state is encoded explicitly rather than silently removing the extra stroke.

F is followed by a straight left angle and detached lower bar, then G prime. The next relation has a curved upper hook and curved lower arm plus a separate lower bar, supporting preceq rather than another straight leq. The last G has no prime. Two small dots at far left are separated from the formula and appear to belong to preceding punctuation.

The complete b) passage is crossed by multiple long diagonal cancellation strokes. Its text reads Pour que F soit une subdivision de G, followed by il f et s. The hyphen after raffine is visible at the right end of the second line, with ment continuing at the left of the third. The third line visibly ends maximal comme; no continuation is supplied. The lower short line begins Ainsi and contains a tentative dans followed by F. A long cancellation stroke crosses that line and turns upward at its right; it is kept inside the same deletion wrapper. The proof line below is outside this deletion.

A continuous horizontal cancellation crosses Ainsi, the short d-initial word and F; it has vertical turns at both ends. Ainsi has a tall capital A, two small raised marks and low connected humps. The next word shows d and a compressed terminal swash, tentatively dans. The final letter has a vertical stem with two transverse strokes, F. The excerpt remains enclosed in deletion because its enclosing passage is cancelled.

The isolated word has a broad initial loop, low v, an i dot, a tall d and a compressed final run ending in a small crossed terminal. Preferred abbreviated évidemt, with évidemment as alternative because the middle minims are not individually separable. It is on the uncancelled proof line.

A tall seriffed I begins the word, followed by low connected strokes and a separate terminal t near the page edge. Inversemt is preferred to the expanded Inversement. A long comma below the terminal is clear. The right edge is the original page boundary, but the terminal t itself is present.

A single dark horizontal stroke cancels the word. A large initial S loop, an i dot and low n-like humps remain; Sinon is preferred but retains doubt under the cancellation. The comma is visible below the right end of the stroke and is included in the cancelled phrase.

Soit stands above the formula. G prime and an opening outer brace are clear; the power-set symbol has a descending stem with a large loop and is rendered calligraphic P. Inside its parentheses L is plain and angular. The condition has A in F, ou, and A equals singleton x; a small looped glyph before that singleton brace is crossed and is read doubtful g/f. The right condition visibly has x, an in-like curved stroke, and |F|. A separate lower mark resembles K but could be a crowded outer closing brace; its state and attachment remain explicit alternatives. The second line has equality, F, a large coproduct, and nested singleton braces. Its lower index reads x in |F| minus |G|; the lowest strokes touch the original image boundary. The visible F-before-G order is preserved without mathematical correction. No unseen closing outer brace is added.

The central crossed glyph lies above/right of the equals sign and just before the opening singleton brace. It has a looped lower hook and diagonal overstroke, tentatively g or f. The opening brace, x and closing brace remain uncancelled. The A at the left is clipped in the narrow crop but is present in the independently inspected overlapping full formula crop S026-19, so the local equality is given complete.

The visible x has crossing diagonals, followed by a curved left stroke with a short detached middle bar, hence in. Vertical bars surround F. Below and to the right is a small vertical-and-two-arms mark resembling K; a crowded closing brace is also possible. It is not silently changed into G or a set difference. Two lower oblique marks at the page corner are separate from the formula and are not treated as mathematical equal signs.

Dém. has an acute accent and one underline. C'est follows with a tall looped C, apostrophe and small est. The word évidemt has compressed minims; suffisant has two prominent f strokes and a dotted i. After the comma the final abbreviated word begins with a seriffed I and ends in t, followed by a comma. The crossed Ainsi line above is only edge context and is not part of this proof-line reading.
